claim.quote: We present the combined results on electron-pair production in 158 GeV/n {Pb-Au} ($\sqrt{s}$= 17.2 GeV) collisions taken at the CERN SPS in 1995 and 1996, and give a detailed account of the data analysis.

name: CERES e+e- pair production in Pb-Au collisions at 158 GeV per nucleon

summary.plain: CERES reported combined 1995-1996 results on electron-positron pairs from lead-gold collisions: more low-mass pairs than expected from hadron decays, by a factor of about 2.3 in semi-central collisions, interpreted as radiation from the dense hadronic medium.
summary.technical: Combined 1995 and 1996 Pb-Au data: enhancement over neutral-meson decays of 2.31 ± 0.19 (stat) ± 0.55 (syst) ± 0.69 (decays) for semi-central collisions (28% of the geometric cross section) integrated over m > 200 MeV/c^2, with stronger-than-linear scaling with N_ch and dominance of low pair pt, suggesting pi+pi- annihilation in a hot dense hadronic medium.

title: e+e- -pair production in Pb-Au collisions at 158 GeV per nucleon
why_it_matters: Established the low-mass dilepton enhancement that motivated the NA60 precision measurement and the interpretation in terms of in-medium rho modification.
